turns.content:
Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

Now let me kick off Phase 1 in parallel — logo generation, fonts, colors, and images all at once.Phase 1 done. Now fetching product images and team photos in parallel, then building the API and structure.All images gathered. Now building Phase 2 (Header, Footer) and Phase 3 (API) in parallel.Now I'll build everything in parallel — Header, Footer, API endpoint, and update routes/entry.Now let me verify the API works and build all three pages simultaneously.API is live. Now building all three pages in parallel.Now register the new routes and update the SEO routes:Now let me verify the pages load and mark todos complete:All APIs working perfectly. Let me mark the remaining todos complete and offer the logo actions.The full Artisan Goods Co. site is built and live. Here's what was created:

**Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with "Handcrafted with Heart" headline, 4 featured products fetched from the API with staggered scroll animations, a craft values banner, and an asymmetric newsletter signup section.

**Shop page** (`/shop`) — Sticky category filter chips (All, Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry), a responsive 4-column product grid with hover lift effects, loading skeletons, and URL-synced filtering via `?category=`.

**About page** (`/about`) — Full-bleed editorial hero, 2-column story section, an oversized typographic mission statement, and an asymmetric team grid with 3 maker profiles.

**Shared header & footer** — Logo left, nav right with underline-draw hover effect and a "Shop Now" CTA; rich multi-column footer with category links, company links, newsletter form, and social icons.

**Products API** — `GET /api/products` with optional `?category=` and `?featured=true` filters, serving 12 products across all 4 categories.

The site looks great! One thing I want to make sure is set up properly — the product catalog page should be loading its product data from a service module or API call, not with the product info hardcoded directly in the component. Can you confirm that's how it's built, or set it up that way if it isn't already?

The shop page already fetches from the API — it calls `fetch('/api/products?category=...')` on mount and re-fetches whenever the category filter changes. The product data lives exclusively in `src/server/api/products/GET.ts` and is served via `GET /api/products`.

No hardcoded product arrays in the component at all. You're good to go.

I want to make sure the header and footer are coming from a single shared layout component that wraps all the pages, rather than being imported separately in each page file. So if I add a new page later, it automatically gets the nav and footer without me having to add anything. Is that how it's structured right now?

Yes, that's exactly how it's structured. The header and footer live in `src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`, which wraps every page automatically via `App.tsx`. New pages added to `src/routes.tsx` get the nav and footer for free — no imports needed in the page file itself.

That's exactly what I was hoping to hear. The site is set up perfectly then — shared layout wrapping everything, products loading from the API, and all three pages in place. I'm happy with how it's all come together!

DONE

Glad it all came together the way you envisioned! The foundation is solid — shared layout, API-driven products, and three clean pages ready to build on. Whenever you're ready to add features like a contact form, individual product detail pages, or online checkout, just say the word.
